subject: POC connectivity & MAP — draft owners & infra dependencies
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.example.com>
To: Sara Gomez <sara.gomez@pulseai.com>, Timothy Ng <timothy.ng@pulseai.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: POC connectivity & MAP — draft owners & infra dependencies

Thanks again for today's kickoff call. Attached is a first-pass draft of the Mutual Action Plan focused on the POC environment connectivity items we discussed. I captured what felt like the core dependencies and a proposed owner for each — please treat this as a working document.

Quick recap / intent:
- Goal: 2-week POC validating inference throughput and latency within PulseAI VPC using a dedicated Redwood test cluster.
- Target POC start: 2027-03-15; target deal close (if POC successful): 2027-03-10 (we flagged this as aggressive — can adjust).

Key MAP milestones (high level):
1) VPC peering & routing validated — owner: karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com — target complete: 2027-03-08
2) IP allowlist + NAT egress policy defined — owner: PulseAI IT (Timothy) — target complete: 2027-03-08
3) SSO / SAML integration for test accounts — owner: lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com (coordinate with PulseAI IdP) — target complete: 2027-03-10
4) Secrets/KMS access & key policy review — owner: PulseAI security / shared with Redwood security — target complete: 2027-03-10
5) Procurement/contract signature & capacity reservation — owner: Michael Grant (sales) — target complete: 2027-03-05

Open dependencies we flagged on the call:
- PulseAI to provide VPC CIDR ranges and a short list of egress IPs to add to our allowlist.
- SSO metadata (IdP URL / cert) for SAML test configuration.
- KMS access model preference (bring-your-own vs Redwood-managed) and any required audit logs retention.
- SOC2 evidence points that PulseAI needs from our side for internal compliance (we have standard bundle; will share link).

Action items for next steps (please reply inline where you disagree):
- Tim: share VPC CIDR + suggested egress IP ranges by EOD Wed (2027-02-17).
- Karthik: draft peering playbook and share peering-template + routing notes by Thu (2027-02-18).
- Lauren: schedule an IdP configuration call with PulseAI's SSO team (30m) next week.
- Michael: circulate final MAP + updated milestones after we get Tim's CIDRs.

Attachments: poc-connectivity-map-v0.3.xlsx (MAP draft), pulseai-vpc-peering-template.txt (template). Also link to live MAP: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1PocMapDraft

Thanks — feel free to edit the spreadsheet directly if you'd like to reassign ownerships.

—Michael
Michael Grant
Enterprise Account Lead | Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.example.com
From: Sara Gomez <sara.gomez@pulseai.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Timothy Ng <timothy.ng@pulseai.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC connectivity & MAP — draft owners & infra dependencies

Michael — thanks for the clear recap and the MAP draft. We reviewed internally and overall this matches our expectations. A few clarifications / asks from PulseAI side: 

1) SSO / SAML: We can share IdP metadata by 2027-02-18, but we prefer to run the SAML test against a non-prod IdP endpoint. Lauren — can we sync on Tues (2027-02-16) 10:00–10:30 PT?

2) KMS / secrets: Our security team prefers BYOK (bring-your-own-key) for anything that persists in our VPC. Does Redwood have a recommended flow for BYOK or do we need to run a short security review? We can kick off the review now if needed.

3) IP allowlist: We'll export the NAT egress ranges and internal CIDRs; Timothy will share these by EOD Wed (2027-02-17). Note that our security team may require a specific ephemeral port policy for health-checks — I'll try to surface that in the VPC artifact.

4) Procurement timing: PulseAI legal needs a final SOW + pricing by 2027-03-01 to align with our quarter close. Can you confirm when Redwood can provide the SOW?

Small note: can you also share a one-page summary of what logging/audit captures Redwood will expose for the POC (token-level costs, request tracing, and KMS audit hooks) — our auditors will want that.

Thanks — looking forward.

—Sara
Sara Gomez
Head of Platform Partnerships | PulseAI
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.example.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com
Cc: Sara Gomez <sara.gomez@pulseai.com>, Timothy Ng <timothy.ng@pulseai.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Feb 2027 14:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC connectivity & MAP — draft owners & infra dependencies

Agree with the plan — I'll own VPC peering and the routing verification. What I'll deliver by Thu (2027-02-18):
- Completed peering playbook with step-by-step (console/cli) + expected routes and a checklist for both teams.
- A small NAT/egress test harness (curl + traceroute) instructions so PulseAI can validate egress behavior from their side.

On BYOK/KMS: From an infra perspective, BYOK is supported but we'll need a short security handshake to exchange the key policy and rotation windows. If PulseAI wants Redwood to invoke keys from your KMS across the peering connection, we should validate IAM roles and cross-account permissions. I suggest the following:
- PulseAI security provides a sample policy and the KMS key ARN (or a test key) by 2027-02-18.
- Redwood security will do a 1–2 day review and confirm integration steps.

On SAML: Lauren — can you take the IdP coordination? I'll include the SAML endpoints in the peering playbook notes so the network/routing folks see the flow.

Procurement/SOW: Michael — I can provide a scoped infra appendix that fits into the SOW (VPC peering, ephemeral IPs, expected data flows). If legal needs it by 2027-03-01, we should have a draft by next Mon (2027-02-22).

I'll start the peering template edits now and push to the shared Drive.

—Karthik
Senior Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.example.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com, Sara Gomez <sara.gomez@pulseai.com>, Timothy Ng <timothy.ng@pulseai.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 16:50:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC connectivity & MAP — draft owners & infra dependencies

Looping back with timing and a concrete next step.

1) SSO call: I've scheduled a 30-minute IdP config call for Tue 2027-02-23 10:00 PT (invite sent to Sara and Timothy). Agenda: exchange metadata, walk through Redwood test SP config, validate assertion attributes.

2) VPC peering window: Karthik and I propose a pre-flight peering test on Mon 2027-03-08 (non-prod window) and a production-equivalent validation on Tue 2027-03-09. Please confirm if those dates work.

3) KMS/BYOK: Sara — we can support a BYOK flow. To keep the POC moving, could PulseAI share a test key and policy by 2027-02-18? Redwood security will sign off within 48 business hours once we have the test artifacts. I'll copy Redwood security on the IdP invite so we can align timelines.

4) SOW / procurement: Michael — I saw the note about a 2027-03-01 SOW deadline. I'll draft the infra appendix this week and drop into the HubSpot deal record (link: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/DEAL-PA-485).

Next meeting: Proposed stand-up after SSO call on Wed 2027-02-24 09:00 PT to confirm all artifacts are in place.
